title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer regional failover ordering and hysteresis
author: Maya Patel
description: Summary: urgent hotfix to stop regional failover thrashing caused by ordering races in the SLO enforcer state transitions and to add hysteresis smoothing. Context: during an elevated traffic event (see incident INC-2026-02-SLO-17) regional SLO enforcers were toggling circuit-breaker state rapidly which triggered cascading regional failovers and increased tail latency for customers on Dedicated clusters. Root cause: concurrent region-state updates in the enforcer could be applied out-of-order under contention, and the existing hysteresis/backoff windows were too short which allowed oscillation. This PR applies a minimal, low-risk hotfix to enforce versioned/CAS updates to region state, tighten ordering guarantees, introduce a short smoothing window and exponential backoff for repeated transitions, and adds integration tests and additional observability. Changes are scoped to the enforcer and failover path only to minimize blast radius. Checklist: - [x] reproduce regression in unit+integration test harness - [x] add CAS-based versioned updates for region state - [x] add hysteresis smoothing window and exponential backoff - [x] add metrics/traces for decision points and publish new dashboards - [x] update runbook with mitigation steps - [x] staged rollout to canary then full (squash merge + immediate deploy to staging canary) Rollout plan: squash-merge, deploy to canary region for 30m, monitor SLO and circuit-breaker metrics, then full rollout. Related: ENG-3892 (root-cause investigation), SRE-210 (runbook), SUP-1123 (support ticket).
